title: Gill Survived Two LBW Appeals on Nought. Then He and Rahul Batted England Out of the Day.
excerpt: India were 0-2 after the first over of their second innings, 311 runs behind. At stumps on Day 4 at Old Trafford, Rahul was 87 not out, Gill 78 not out, and the series was alive.
body:
At 11:06 AM on Saturday at Old Trafford, Chris Woakes had India at 0-2. Both Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sai Sudharsan were caught in the slips off successive deliveries. England’s supporters, still buzzing from Ben Stokes’ extraordinary century and a first-innings total of 669, could almost taste a 3-1 series lead.

Then Shubman Gill and KL Rahul walked out and refused to leave.

## The Crisis

India had been bowled out for 358 in their first innings, with Stokes — who had not scored a Test century in more than two years — taking 5-72 and then smashing 141 in England’s reply. His hundred was punctuated by a reverse-sweep off Washington Sundar, a six off Ravindra Jadeja, and a crooked finger pointed skyward in memory of his late father Ged.

England’s 669 was their fifth-highest Test total of all time. India trailed by 311. With the series at 2-1 in England’s favour and two matches remaining, a collapse here would hand the hosts a decisive lead.

Woakes almost ended it before it began. Two balls, two edges, two wickets, and India’s top order had evaporated.

## The Fightback

Gill arrived at the crease on a hat-trick ball. He survived it. Then Jofra Archer rapped him on the pads in the second ball after lunch — an impassioned LBW appeal that was turned down, the review inconclusive. Two runs later, Archer struck him on the pad again. Another appeal. Another not-out call. The ball was shown to be missing off stump.

“That was the decisive passage,” former India coach Ravi Shastri said on Sky Sports. “If Gill goes there, India are three down for nothing and the game is over by tea.”

Instead, Gill hit back. A cut and a straight drive off Woakes — two boundaries in three balls that signalled a shift in intent. He survived a dropped catch at point by Liam Dawson off Brydon Carse on 46, then accelerated. A three off Joe Root’s part-time spin brought up a 77-ball fifty.

At the other end, Rahul was immovable. His approach was the mirror image of Gill’s — patient, watchful, building his innings on a foundation of solid defence. But he showed aggression when Archer strayed, dispatching a late cut and a forceful pull. His fifty came off 141 balls.

## The Numbers

At stumps, India were 174-2. The deficit was down to 137. The unbroken third-wicket stand between Gill (78*) and Rahul (87*) had spanned the entire afternoon and evening sessions.

Stokes, crucially, did not bowl himself — a concerning sign for England given his history of hamstring trouble. Without their captain’s pace, England’s attack lacked the penetration to dislodge two batters who had decided that survival was everything.

For Gill, it was a return to the form that had defined the start of the series. He had scored three centuries in four innings — a masterclass that included a career-best 269 at Edgbaston — before a lean patch of 34 runs in three knocks. The pressure of captaincy, the English conditions, and the scrutiny of leading India without Bumrah in the XI for two of those matches had weighed on him.

“He’s composed, he’s very regal,” Shastri said. “He has the ability to play the long innings. He’s right up there.”

## What Comes Next

Day 5 resumes on Sunday with India needing 137 more runs to make England bat again. The equation is simple: if Gill and Rahul survive the new ball, India have a realistic chance of saving the Test. If England break through early, the lower order will be exposed and the series could effectively be decided.

The fifth and final Test is at The Oval. But for India’s travelling fans — and the millions watching across time zones — Old Trafford’s Day 4 was a reminder of why Test cricket endures. Two batters. One crisis. An entire day of defiance.
